title: Takht Keshgarh Sahib
hookLine: at Anandpur, where the Khalsa was born

lines: PLACE OF BIRTH: A CITY ON A FORM.
A BIRTHPLACE NO FORM ASKS FOR.
ONE HILL, FOR EVERY NEW SIKH.
cards: A form asks for your place of birth, and you write a city. Then the form moves on. But a week ago, in the instructions after amrit, the newly initiated were told something about their birthplace that no form asks for.
Their spiritual father, Guru Gobind Singh. Their spiritual mother, Mata Sahib Kaur. Their home, Anandpur.
And their birthplace: not a hospital or a city, but one particular hill and the gurdwara on it. Anyone who takes amrit, in any country, is told they were born there.

teach.b: Anandpur sits in the foothills of Punjab, and its name means the city of bliss.

teach.h: WHERE TRADITION SAYS THE KHALSA BEGAN.
teach.b: Sikh tradition says it was here, at the Vaisakhi gathering this path has told before, that Guru Gobind Singh called for the five, gave them amrit, and founded the Khalsa.

Takht Keshgarh Sahib stands at the place tradition remembers for that day. It's one of the five Takhts the Ardas remembers, and it's tied to one event: the birth of the Khalsa. Hold three things together.
First, the place: a hill, a white gurdwara, the town below. Ordinary ground that tradition says became the ground of a beginning. Second, the code's sentence.
The Sikh Rehat Maryada has the five tell each person who takes amrit that their birthplace is Keshgarh Sahib. That turns a site on a map into a family address.
A Sikh taking amrit in Toronto or Nairobi is told the same as one taking it at Anandpur itself: you were born on that hill. Third, the weapons.

teach.h: THE GURU'S ARMS, KEPT AND SHOWN.
teach.b: Tradition says arms associated with Guru Gobind Singh are kept at Keshgarh Sahib and shown to the sangat, among them a khanda, the double-edged sword, the kind used to stir the amrit. So the Takht's work becomes clear.
The Akal Takht is where the panth speaks.
Keshgarh Sahib is where the Khalsa remembers being born. Every amrit ceremony, wherever it happens, points back up that hill.

how: Takht Keshgarh Sahib at Anandpur marks the place Sikh tradition remembers as the Khalsa's birthplace; the Sikh Rehat Maryada has the newly initiated told that Keshgarh Sahib is their birthplace.

o: the Takht at Anandpur, where tradition says the Khalsa began
the Takht at Amritsar where Sikh edicts are written and sent
the gurdwara where the first Granth was compiled by hand

games.q: you've just taken amrit in Toronto. the five tell you your birthplace. what do they say?
games.why: the code has every newly initiated Sikh told the same birthplace: Keshgarh Sahib, where tradition says the Khalsa was born.

practice: See low hills, green and brown, a town gathered at their feet, and a white gurdwara with a flag above it on one rise, and slow your breathing to the pace of a crowd climbing toward it on a spring morning.
Then, gently, bring to mind the place where something began for you, not where you were born but where you started becoming who you are, and rest there.

wordCard.voice: Takht Keshgarh Sahib. The Takht at Anandpur, where tradition says the Khalsa was born, and the birthplace every new member of the Khalsa is given. Today's word.
